title: bls12-381-fixed-g1-invert-g2: bounded distinguished-point rho in GT

claims.statement: For a uniform nonidentity P in BLS12-381 G1 and an independent uniform z in GT, the fixed-budget attack in proof.md returns Q=[a]Q0 in G2 with e(P,Q)=z under the pinned pairing convention, using at most 2^127.80 total target-group-operation equivalents (dense Fp12 multiplications, C=20,000). It computes g=e(P,Q0) and solves z=g^a by a van Oorschot-Wiener parallel distinguished-point Pollard rho on the cyclic group GT of prime order r, with a HARD global charged-work cutoff W_max=ceil(1.25*k0) total multiplications (k0=sqrt(2*r*ln(1/0.61))): the attack performs at most W_max multiplications and stops, so every walk, restart, truncated-segment and exceptional-path multiplication is inside W_max. There is no automorphism; the structural fruitless cycles of orbit walks are absent, and the only remaining exceptional events are random-mapping trajectories that enter a distinguished-point-free cycle, which occur with probability ~2^-92 per walk and are handled by per-walk truncation at 2^36 steps. Each step is one dense Fp12 multiplication plus ~300 scalar instructions; 1.015 units per step; theta=2^-30 distinguished-point density; cheap D*M_j restarts. The bounded success probability is at least 1-0.61^1.5625 minus ~2^-90 of exceptional loss, i.e. >= 0.39, under the random-mapping heuristic, supported by toy experiments measuring collision within the hard cutoff. Peak memory is bounded hard by a fixed 2^100-slot distinguished-point table (record count mean 2^97.74, exceeds 2^100 only with doubly-exponentially small probability by Chernoff, not binding before the collision): at most 2^108 bytes. Preprocessing is at most 2^32 units and is included; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. This is a classical cold attack with no uncharged advice or quantum steps; generic square-root accounting, not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Faithful bounded implementation: parallel R-adding distinguished-point rho on a prime-order-l subgroup of F_q^* (cyclic, standing in for GT) with a HARD global cutoff W_max=ceil(1.25*k0) and per-walk truncation. Counts every group multiplication; reports the fraction of trials finding a usable collision WITHIN W_max (a Monte-Carlo estimate of the bounded success probability) and the mean per-trial truncations. Toy-scale evidence for the random-mapping collision-time model and the bounded algorithm only.
